text:
Alex Potts: taking over night shift — I'm primary for the next 8h. brief: INC-7893 (embeddings path) is active, customers A,B,C seeing elevated tail latency and intermittent 429s. handing off from @Sara Kim.

Sara Kim: quick recap — started at 23:10 UTC. root symptoms: embeddings queue length spiked after a client rollout; queue processor pods saturated, retry/backpressure cascaded into upstream routing which caused model fallback churn.

incident-bot: [ALERT] INC-7893 triggered at 2026-11-12T23:07:45Z — embeddings-processor.p95 latency > 800ms, error rate 5% > threshold. Pager sent to #eng-oncall.

Miguel Hernandez: current status — autoscaling tried to spin up 3 extra embeddings worker pods but they failed healthchecks twice (OOMKilled). logs show memory growth in `embed-worker` during large-batch ingestion.

Lia Chen: customer impact: large enterprise customers (A, B) see request timeouts at ~10% rate for batch embedding jobs > 256 tokens. Small queries (< 64 tokens) mostly ok. We have a couple of support tickets. No major revenue-severe impacts yet but SLA risk for bulk jobs.

Priya Rao: mitigations in progress: 1) temporarily enabled routing fallback to lower-capacity model (embedding-compact) for non-critical customers (config: `route:embedding->embedding-compact`), 2) scaled up dedicated embeddings pool (manually added 4 g4dn nodes), 3) disabled batch coalescing for 10m to reduce memory spikes.

Alex Potts: actions I've taken on join: 1) confirmed `route` change is live (trace id 0f3a7), 2) bumped replicas for embed-worker to 8 with `kubectl scale deploy/embed-worker --replicas=8` (see infra-bot validation below), 3) opened a limited-rate gate for heavy clients via `quota:client-heavy -> 20rps`.

infra-bot: kubectl scale returned: deployment.apps/embed-worker scaled to 8 replicas — new pods pending, 4/8 ready after 120s. Node autoscaler request issued to cloud provider.

Sara Kim: observed side-effect — fallback to embedding-compact increases per-request latency slightly but reduces peak memory pressure. Good short-term win.

Miguel Hernandez: logs snippet from crashed pod (tail -n 50):
```
2026-11-12T22:58:12Z ERROR embed-worker out-of-memory: Java heap space
2026-11-12T22:58:12Z WARN processing batch size=512 tokens=10240
2026-11-12T22:58:12Z INFO received request from client-id=enterprise-A trace=0f3a7
```

Lia Chen: I've notified support and product leads, sent a short note to customer A that we're mitigating and will follow up. saving escalation until we see persistence after scale.

Priya Rao: we should run the runbook step `embeddings-memory-spike` if we see >3 pod restarts in 30m. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-memory-spike (ops-only).

Alex Potts: identified a coverage gap: night team currently doesn't have direct access to the internal model profiling dashboard (needs SSO approval). Lia — can you confirm access for miguel/alex?

Lia Chen: will request SSO grant now, ETA ~30m.

Miguel Hernandez: next debug steps (I'm on it): attach to one of the new pods, collect heap dump and profiler, and check if there is a particular batch size or client causing leak. I'll start with `kubectl exec -it embed-worker-7 -- jcmd GC.heap_info` then upload to /tmp/emb-heap.

Sara Kim: tickets/alerts to watch: 
- pagerduty INC-7893 (active)
- grafana: embeddings-queue-length (alerting rule `EQL-emb-queue-high`)
- cloud: node-autoscaler-failed (info)

Alex Potts: temporary playbook summary for next on-call: 
- Primary: Alex Potts (me) — triage & mitigation
- Secondary: Miguel Hernandez — debugging & heap dumps
- Backup: Priya Rao — routing/quota changes
- Keep Lia Chen in loop for customer comms/SSO

Alex Potts: explicit next steps before handoff: 
1) confirm new pods stabilise (aim 8/8 ready) — target within 25m
2) validate that 429s drop below 1% and p95 latency < 400ms for embeddings
3) if pods keep OOMing, revert batch size to 128 server-side and re-enable coalescing throttled to low throughput
4) collect heap dump and open GH issue with profiler artifacts

Priya Rao: note about rollout gating — we should block client A heavy batches with `quota` until we've validated stability (I've set gate to 20rps already). If you need to widen gate, coordinate here.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] INC-7893 mitigations applied by Alex, Priya; monitoring for recovery.

Miguel Hernandez: update at +25m: new pods stabilized 8/8 ready, memory utilization steady at 62% on new nodes. Observed one small restart for embed-worker-2 at +12m, reason: imagePullBackOff (transient).

Lia Chen: customer comms sent to A & B: short update and ETA for follow-up in 2 hours.

Alex Potts: closing notes for this leg of the shift — overall risk reduced but not fully resolved (root cause likely large-batch memory growth). if anyone pages overnight, follow the runbook and escalate to infra pager if autoscaler fails again. I'll hand over to @Miguel at 02:00 UTC for deeper memory analysis.

Miguel Hernandez: ack, I'll take watch at 02:00 UTC. I'll be focusing on heap dumps and whether batch coalescing code path leaks on big batches.

Priya Rao: leaving a saved query for watch: `sum(rate(embedding_errors[5m])) by (client)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(embedding_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))`.

Alex Potts: thanks team — leave any notes here. I'll update thread if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

Priya Rao: one quick Q — should we revert fallback for non-critical clients after 1h if stable? leaning yes, but prefer to wait until heap dumps analysed.

Alex Potts: agree wait. we'll aim for a controlled rollback once we confirm no OOMs in 2h.

incident-bot: [RESUME MONITORING] INC-7893 — next automatic update in 30m.
